title: bale per-session telemetry record
description: Shape of claude/telemetry/<sid>.json — the durable per-session record bale writes at session close: every apply-close event (v0.3.9, session B2; BALE.md section 8.9) and, since v0.3.16, every `bale unlock` close (BALE.md section 9.3), so every registry close is a recorded event — and, since v0.3.18, every clean `bale rollback` / `bale rollback --undo` (BALE.md section 9.2): post-close history events that append to the sid's existing record rather than opening a closure. One file per sid; each apply-close event appends an entry to attempts[] rather than duplicating the file, so a HOLD followed by a retry accumulates both. INTENTIONALLY LOOSE, matching diagnostics.schema.json: additionalProperties is true at the top level and inside attempts[] entries so future fields can be added without breaking earlier aggregation across sessions (board 5 reads these longitudinally). record_version is the versioned evolution hook: bump it when a change is not purely additive; consumers filter or branch on it. v0.4.6 (board 10 S5) lands three additive extensions, record_version stays 1: the attempts[].cost block (mechanical stream, all-null until the harness era), the no_response / malformed_response closure reasons, and the optional claim_basis field on claim-bearing rows (enum predicted | observed — enforced record-wide by validate_telemetry_record in bin/bale_validate.py, the per-record library entry point added alongside).

record_version.description: Version of the record shape. 1 is the B2 launch shape. Additive fields do not bump it; shape-breaking changes do.

session_id.description: The session this record describes. Matches the filename stem and the response manifest's responds_to.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the first attempt written. Preserved across updates.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the most recent attempt written.

outcome.description: The latest attempt's outcome, mirrored to the envelope so aggregation can filter without descending into attempts[]. 'applied' = merged; 'held' = HOLD awaiting inspection (a later attempt supersedes it); 'reverted' = backed out (walkthrough revert or `bale revert`); 'rejected' = the apply exited through a pre-flight or pipeline error path (detail in the session log); 'bailout' = response_kind=bailout, session consumed; 'scope-drift-refused' = the own-scope drift gate refused the response's changes[] at apply pre-flight (BALE.md section 8.1 step 14; v0.3.10, additive enum value) — the session stays open, so a later attempt supersedes it the way a HOLD's does; 'required-check-refused' = the required-check superset gate refused at apply pre-flight because validation_will_run omits name(s) the project's [validation] required set demands (BALE.md section 8.1 step 15; board 6 session B, additive enum value — record_version stays 1, the scope-drift-refused precedent) — the session stays open, same supersession posture; 'unlocked' = the session was closed by `bale unlock` with no git side effects (BALE.md section 9.3; v0.3.16, additive enum value) — the attempt's closure_reason carries why; 'rolled-back' = an applied (merged) session was undone by `bale rollback` via history-preserving `git revert` (BALE.md section 9.2; v0.3.18, additive enum value); 're-applied' = a prior rollback was reversed by `bale rollback --undo` (v0.3.18, additive enum value) — both are post-close history events appended to the sid's existing record, stamped only on the clean-success paths that write the reverted/<sid> / re-applied/<sid> tags.

attempts.description: One entry per apply-close event against this sid, in order. HOLD-then-retry appends rather than duplicates; the full attempt history is the point — a HOLD attempt's claim/verdict disagreement is calibration data even after a later attempt merges.

at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of this apply-close event.

outcome.description: This attempt's outcome, same vocabulary as the envelope field.

command.description: Which bale command produced the event. Walkthrough reverts inside apply/retry report that command; `bale revert <sid>` reports 'revert'; `bale unlock` reports 'unlock' (v0.3.16, additive enum value); `bale pack --supersedes` reports 'pack' on the parent's superseded-by-split closure (v0.3.17, additive enum value) — the record honestly names the command that produced the event, with outcome 'unlocked' (the registry-close outcome, whatever command drove it); `bale rollback` reports 'rollback' on its clean-success paths (v0.3.18, additive enum value), with outcome 'rolled-back' or 're-applied'.

closure_reason.description: Why the session closed, stamped on unlock and revert events (v0.3.16, additive nullable field; absent on pre-v0.3.16 attempts). Two harness-anticipating values land in v0.4.6 (board 10 S5, additive enum values — record_version stays 1, the scope-drift-refused precedent): 'no_response' = a request went out and nothing came back — the worker-silence case, closed on timeout; 'malformed_response' = a response arrived that could not be applied as a response — distinct from a well-formed response that HOLDs. Both are CLI-accepted from v0.4.6 (`bale unlock --reason` / `bale revert --reason`) and expected to stay empty until a harness produces the events (orchestration.md section 9's worker-refresh doctrine); the respawn mechanics they anticipate are S6 design, not this vocabulary's. This enum is deliberately CLOSED (no unknown values validate) — the one strict spot in an intentionally loose record, because the closure mix aggregation buckets on these strings; validate_telemetry_record (bin/bale_validate.py, v0.4.6) additionally enforces the vocabulary record-wide, so a closure_reason key riding at any other depth gets the same verdict (known reason or null passes; an invented value rejects wherever it appears). Unlock stamps it always: the operator's --reason when given; else 'closed-read-only' when the recorded scope is exactly [] (the v0.3.15 read-only session shape — an explicit --reason beats the inference, since a read-only session can itself be superseded or abandoned-in-fact); else 'abandoned'. The no-sid crash-debris sweep stamps 'crash-debris'. Revert stamps --reason when given and null otherwise — outcome 'reverted' already names the event, and a null reason is honest rather than a guessed one. `bale pack --supersedes` stamps 'superseded-by-split' with command 'pack' on the parent's close (v0.3.17). The read-only sweep stamps 'closed-read-only' with command 'pack' (v0.3.21, board 33): a `bale pack --read-only` that finds an open []-scope session offers to close it at an accept-default prompt (piped stdin declines without a prompt), so the value is both unlock's inferred reason and a pack-stamped one. Null on apply/retry attempts: those are apply-close events, not closures. Null on rollback attempts too (v0.3.18): rollback closes no session — the outcome names the event, matching revert's null-when-no---reason posture.

tarball.description: Basename of the response tarball this attempt processed, or null when no tarball was in play (the `bale revert` path).

validation.description: What validation.sh found on this attempt, or null when it did not run (rejected before staging, bailout, `bale revert`).

state.description: PASS when validation.sh exited 0, HOLD otherwise (BALE.md section 8.6).

exit_code.description: validation.sh's exit code (TARBALL.md section 7.5: 0 pass, 1 check failed, 2 script errored).

claim_basis.description: See claim_verdict's claim_basis — same field, same closed enum, on the prediction side's annotated form.

claims.description: The manifest's claims map verbatim — the prediction side of the TARBALL.md section 5.3 split. Values are the bare claim string ('pass', 'fail', 'untested', 'unknown'), or — from v0.4.6 (board 10 S5) — an annotated object form a claim-bearing row may take, admitting the optional claim_basis field (enum exactly predicted | observed; see claim_verdict's claim_basis for the semantics). Optional everywhere, no backfill: every legacy bare-string value keeps validating, and validate_telemetry_record (bin/bale_validate.py) additionally rejects any claim_basis value outside the enum wherever in the record it appears.

claim_verdict.description: Per-check agreement parsed from validation.sh's section 7.3 reconciliation block — the promotion of what previously lived only in the transient .bale/logs/ session log. Keys are check names; values carry the claim, the verdict, and the agreement tag as the block reported them.

agreement.description: The bracketed tag from the reconciliation line, normalized to lowercase without brackets: 'agree', 'disagree', or 'n/a'.

claim_basis.description: SELF-REPORTED STREAM (v0.4.6, board 10 S5 — the section 3 watch's closure, ratified 2026-08-03's claim-basis precedent): did the worker predict this claim's outcome from structural grounds, or observe it from a real run before shipping. Optional on every claim-bearing row, everywhere it appears; no backfill (absent on every pre-S5 record, deliberately); no read side at S5. When present the enum is CLOSED — predicted and observed are the whole vocabulary, the second of exactly two strict spots in this loose record, because the ledger's predicted-vs-observed calibration split is only meaningful over a fixed vocabulary. validate_telemetry_record (bin/bale_validate.py) enforces the enum record-wide, on any row of any claim-bearing surface, so an invented basis rejects wherever it rides.

reconciliation_parsed.description: True when a section 7.3 'claims vs verdict:' block was found and parsed from validation.sh's output. False means claim_verdict is empty because the block was absent or unrecognizable — validation.sh authors the block per convention, not contract, so a parse miss is recorded rather than silently skipped.

checkpoint.description: Board 6 session A: the blind checkpoint's result on this attempt (BALE.md section 8.5). Key-presence semantics — the reconciliation_parsed / clarification disambiguation doctrine applied a third time: the key is PRESENT on every validated attempt written post-epoch and ABSENT otherwise (pre-epoch records, and attempts where validation.sh did not run), so aggregation never conflates 'no checkpoint configured' with 'pre-epoch no data'. {"configured": false} is the known-zero form. Blind outcomes never merge into validation.claim_verdict: the checkpoint has no claims by construction, and a merged row would fabricate a prediction that was never made.

configured.description: True when the merged config's [validation] base named a checkpoint and it executed on this attempt; false is the known-zero form — validation ran with no checkpoint pinned.

state.description: The checkpoint script's OWN state: PASS on exit 0, HOLD otherwise. The attempt's overall validation.state requires both scripts' exit 0 for PASS (BALE.md section 8.6); this field carries the per-source attribution.

exit_code.description: The checkpoint's exit code (TARBALL.md section 7.5: 0 pass, 1 check failed, 2 the script itself errored — surfaced as 'the planner's checkpoint itself errored', since the remedy differs from a worker failure).

script.description: Identity of the EXECUTED bytes: the repo-relative configured path and the sha256 of the base-tree blob (git show <base_sha>:<path>) that actually ran — never the staged overlay's copy. This hash is what makes the provenance verification auditable after the fact.

stamp_matched.description: The BALE.md section 8.5 provenance verification's result (v0.3.28, board 6 session C): true when the executed base-tree bytes matched the request manifest's pack-time provenance.checkpoint stamp; false when a divergence was admitted by --accept-checkpoint-change (the current base-tree version ran); null when the request carried no provenance.checkpoint key (hand-rolled requests, and requests packed pre-0.3.28).

scope_kind.description: The write-forecast epoch key (v0.4.2, ADR-0015 board 13 session B — the reconciliation_parsed disambiguation doctrine applied a fourth time). PRESENT on every attempt written post-epoch and ABSENT before: key presence is epoch membership, so aggregation never averages pre-separation drift rates (scope = the conflated include set; drift structurally near zero) against forecast-era ones (scope = the write forecast; drift expected nonzero by design — judgment past the ask). Stamped unconditionally by build_telemetry_attempt on every command's attempts, so no per-call-site branching can desync the epoch. The one value today names the one post-epoch meaning; record_version stays 1 (additive), and `bale stats` computes its forecast rows over attempts carrying this key only.

scope.description: The session's recorded scope, raw. Post-separation (ADR-0015 — attempts carrying scope_kind) this is the session's WRITE FORECAST: what the session forecast landing, which the drift the aggregation computes from scope vs change_paths grades as judgment past the ask. Pre-separation attempts (no scope_kind key) recorded the conflated resolved include set — the 'includes shipped' side of the includes-vs-changes comparison — and open sessions packed pre-separation read as over-forecasts. Empty when no scope was recorded (pre-ADR-0007 sessions), for the read-only session shape (the empty forecast), and on rollback attempts when the session directory (and its scope.json) is long gone at rollback time (v0.3.18): [] records 'not recoverable' honestly, never a fabricated whole-tree scope.

overridden_paths.description: Out-of-scope changes[] paths a per-invocation `bale apply --allow-out-of-scope` admitted past the own-scope drift gate on this attempt (v0.3.10, additive field; BALE.md section 8.1 step 14). Bale-computed, always a list: empty means no override was in play (including every pre-v0.3.10 attempt, where the key is absent). On a scope-drift-refused attempt it carries what a PARTIAL override admitted while other drift still refused; the refused paths are recoverable from scope vs change_paths, both recorded raw.

required_check_overrides.description: Required check NAMES a per-invocation `--allow-missing-required-check` admitted past the required-check superset gate on this attempt (board 6 session B, additive field; BALE.md section 8.1 step 15) — the overridden_paths mirror, with the gate's own unit: check names, not paths. Bale-computed, always a list: empty means no override was in play (including every pre-session-B attempt, where the key is absent). On a required-check-refused attempt it carries what a PARTIAL override admitted while other missing names still refused.

sandbox_escaped.description: True when this attempt's response scripts (apply.sh, the blind checkpoint, validation.sh) executed UNCONFINED under a per-invocation --no-sandbox (v0.4.5, board 10 S2 — ADR-0016 position 2's loud escape, promoted from the session log's FORCE line to a durable stamp). Bale-computed and stamped unconditionally by build_telemetry_attempt on every post-S2 attempt of every command — key presence is epoch membership (the overridden_paths posture: uniform shape, absent only on pre-S2 records), and false is the known-negative form, including attempts where no script ran at all (unlock, pack, rollback, rejected-before-staging — nothing executed, so nothing escaped). The escape's use frequency is itself the telemetry signal ADR-0016 flagged worth watching. Not in required: pre-S2 records keep validating.

network_grant_exercised.description: True when at least one confined script execution on this attempt ran with the project's network grant active — bale.toml [sandbox] network (project layer only), which makes bale pass network=True so the sandbox omits its --net leg while filesystem confinement and the environment scrub stay intact (v0.4.5, board 10 S2 — ADR-0016 position 3: planner-granted, per-project, contract-only, recorded whenever exercised). Bale-computed and stamped unconditionally like sandbox_escaped above — key presence is epoch membership, false is the known-negative form. An escaped (--no-sandbox) attempt records false here even when the grant is configured: nothing confined ran, so no grant was exercised (unconfined scripts have network regardless). Write-only at S2 per the ratified deferral — the bale stats read side lands when data accrues. Not in required: pre-S2 records keep validating.

cost.description: What this attempt's worker session spent (v0.4.6, board 10 S5 — Addition B's day-one piece; orchestration.md section 10's cost-governance doctrine). MECHANICAL STREAM ONLY: the harness writes these, humans never do — spend is never a worker self-estimate. Stamped unconditionally by build_telemetry_attempt on every post-S5 attempt of every command as the all-null block — key presence is epoch membership (the sandbox_escaped posture: uniform shape, absent only on pre-S5 records), and all-null is the expected steady state until the harness era populates real values. The epoch boundary is the point: records born from S5 forward carry the shape, so no second backfill era, and cost records cover every session exit — the apply-only corpus lesson applied in advance. Every field nullable; the block itself admits null for symmetry with the other nullable promoted surfaces. Not in required: pre-S5 records keep validating. Write-only at S5 per the ratified deferral — the `bale stats` read side lands when data accrues.

tokens_in.description: Input tokens the worker session consumed, or null when unmeasured (every pre-harness session).

tokens_out.description: Output tokens the worker session produced, or null when unmeasured.

usd.description: Dollar cost of the worker session, or null when unmeasured.

model_tier.description: The model tier the spawn ran on (orchestration.md section 10: tier is an effort-policy allocation), or null when unrecorded.

change_paths.description: Every changes[].path in the response manifest — the other side of the includes-vs-changes comparison. Aggregation computes the intersection or drift; the record stores both sides raw.

feedback.description: The response manifest's feedback block, verbatim (response-manifest.schema.json, v0.3.8 B1). Null when the manifest carried none (pre-B1 responses) or when the manifest was unavailable (some rejected paths).

diagnostics.description: The bailout's diagnostics.json content, verbatim (v0.3.23, board 5 D1 — additive; record_version stays 1). Present on bailout attempts only: apply's bailout close already holds the parsed, schema-validated diagnostics in hand and embeds them symmetrically with feedback, promoting the transient .bale/sessions/<sid>/ copy's key facts to the tracked substrate stats reads. Absent on every other attempt and on all pre-v0.3.23 bailout attempts — key absence means the record predates the embed, never that diagnostics were empty.

clarification.description: Bale-computed summary of .bale/clarifications/<sid>/ stamped at close time (v0.3.23, board 5 D1 — additive; record_version stays 1). Present on every post-epoch CLOSING attempt — outcomes applied, reverted, bailout, unlocked, whatever command drove the close — and on no other: held, scope-drift-refused, rejected, and rollback attempts are not closures. The always-stamp rule is the point: key presence with rounds: 0 means KNOWN ZERO (bale looked and found no clarification records on this checkout), while key absence means pre-epoch unknown — the reconciliation_parsed disambiguation doctrine applied to a new field, so aggregation never conflates 'no clarifications' with 'no data'. A clarification response itself still writes no record (it suspends, not closes — BALE.md section 8.10.2); the stamp is how the rounds reach the ledger when the session eventually closes.

rounds.description: Number of preserved clarification records — len(records). Since v0.4.18 this is the exchange thread's length: every preserved record on either side (worker rounds and planner answers alike, BALE.md section 8.11), not only worker rounds.

n.description: The round number from the record's NNN filename.

at.description: The record's own preserved_at stamp when present (v0.3.27 — stamped by apply at preservation time, since mtime survives normal use but not every copy/restore path), else the record file's mtime as ISO 8601 UTC (the fallback for pre-v0.3.27 records, which carry no stamp of their own — deliberately not backfilled). Null when neither is available.

blocking_questions.description: len(questions) from the preserved manifest; null when the record would not parse — presence still counts as a round (the file is the suspension fact), only the count degrades.

from.description: Additive (v0.4.18, the exchange thread — BALE.md section 8.11, ADR-0017; record_version stays 1): the side that wrote the record. A preserved clarification manifest reads as 'worker'; an exchange record carries its own `from`. Null when the record would not parse or names neither side. Absent on pre-v0.4.18 stamps.

answers.description: Additive (v0.4.18): len(answers) from the record, or null when the record carries no answers[] (every pre-thread manifest) or would not parse — null, not zero, so aggregation tells 'asked only' from 'answered nothing'. Absent on pre-v0.4.18 stamps.

superseded_by.description: The child session id, stamped by `bale pack --supersedes` onto the parent's superseded-by-split closure attempt once the child sid is minted (v0.3.23, board 5 D4 — additive; record_version stays 1). Single-writer: the same pack invocation that wrote the closure enriches it, so no cross-session write timing and no apply-side append. Present only on that closure attempt; absent everywhere else, including the one pre-v0.3.23 split record, which is deliberately not backfilled (its edge survives in git history). An aborted supersession pack's idempotent re-run re-stamps the same attempt in place — the completing pack's child sid wins.

log.description: Repo-relative path to the session log where full validation output and rejection detail live.
